concept: Perp maker taker fees funding payments and borrow interest as costs

claims.text: The JLP-market price impact fee has two parts. The linear part rounds up to whole basis points, so every trade pays at least 0.01%; at October 2026 parameters SOL adds 0.01% per started ~$375,000 of size. The additive part applies only when a trade enlarges the roughly one-minute net long-minus-short flow beyond a per-asset threshold ($1.5M on SOL and ETH, $750,000 on wBTC). Base, linear and additive fees together cap at 0.50% of trade size, so the price impact fee is at most 0.44%. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jupiter's JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC) charge no funding rate. A trader pays a borrow fee on the full position size for as long as the position is open. The fee accrues without compounding and is settled from collateral when the position changes or closes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

When Velocity's longs and shorts are unbalanced, its AMM takes the other side of the leftover. In each funding period the AMM may spend at most one third of its retained equity on asymmetric funding, it never draws on the insurance fund for a funding shortfall, and it may widen its quote on the side it pays. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Splitting a large order within one minute on Jupiter's JLP markets does not avoid the additive price impact fee. The fee measures all net flow on the asset over roughly the last minute, including the trader's own trades and liquidations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Holding costs eat margin. Pacifica deducts funding from an isolated position's margin balance and recalculates its liquidation price after each payout. Jupiter's accrued borrow fees count against collateral, so the liquidation price drifts toward the market even when the position is untouched. (medium confidence)

Pacifica funding is sampled every 5 seconds and the average is applied hourly. The rate is the premium index plus a clamped adjustment toward a fixed 0.01% interest rate, divided by 8. It is capped at plus or minus 4% per hour. Positive funding means longs pay shorts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Cost-model rule for a held perp position: JLP-market cost is the open and close fees plus price impact plus the borrow fee times hours open (about $0.16/hour per $10,000 at the docs' illustrative 0.0016%/hour). A funding venue's cost is the maker or taker fees plus signed funding, which can be a credit. Compare them over the intended holding time, not by headline fee alone. (medium confidence)

A JLP-market liquidation takes all remaining collateral after the loss, the close fee and the borrow fees. A Beta-market liquidation instead charges a 0.75% to 1% fee on position value (the liquidation price also allows for the 0.035% taker fee) and returns whatever collateral remains, which in a fast market can be little or nothing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Velocity divides each taker fee in a fixed order. The referee discount, filler (keeper) reward, referrer reward and maker rebate come off first. The remainder splits 15% to the AMM, 15% to the insurance fund and 70% to the protocol on mainnet's live configuration; both shares are admin-settable. Spot fills and direct swaps charge no trading fee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

On Velocity, a fill can cost more than the tier number for traceable reasons. A market can be priced above the schedule (a market 1.5 bps above a 5 bps tier costs 6.5 bps), and a builder fee (capped at 1% of notional) is charged on top of the taker fee. Both are set onchain and readable. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Velocity aims to charge longs and shorts the same funding rate, but its AMM takes the leftover imbalance. The AMM may spend at most one third of its retained equity per funding period on asymmetric funding; past that, the paying side's rate is capped and receipts are scaled to what is available. The insurance fund is never drawn on to cover a funding shortfall. The premium is capped at 3% of oracle TWAP for contract tiers A and B, 5% for tier C and 10% below. A per-market dead zone and ramp slope shape the rate between the oracle floor and the cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Liquidation is a fee event, not only a close. On Jupiter JLP markets all remaining collateral is taken as the liquidation fee after the loss, close fee and borrow fees. On Beta markets the forced close pays the 0.035% taker fee plus a liquidation fee of 0.75% (crypto) or 1% (stock markets) and what remains is returned, which in a fast market can be little or nothing. GUM charges each liquidation close the taker fee plus a liquidation fee, never more than the sub-account holds. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jupiter Beta market rates: maker 0.005% (limit orders that rest), taker 0.035% (market and immediately-filled limit orders), liquidation fee 0.75% on crypto markets and 1% on stock markets. The page says the trading engine can adjust these. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jupiter's Beta-market page lists a 0.005% (0.5 bps) maker fee on limit orders that rest on the book, a 0.035% (3.5 bps) taker fee on market orders and on limit orders that execute immediately, and a liquidation fee of 0.75% of position value on JUP, HYPE and ZEC and 1% on the stock markets. The page says the trading engine can adjust these rates. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jupiter's two risk advisers justify the JLP fees differently. Gauntlet models a trading fee as (base fee + order-book impact) x trade size and treats the borrow rate as cost-of-carry for warehousing inventory (delta and time risk). Chaos Labs argues JLP providers also bear manipulation, redemption and directional risk and cannot hedge as a market maker can, so they need a higher premium. Jupiter's developer docs say it works with both firms to tune the borrow-fee parameters. (medium confidence)

On Velocity, a resting limit order without the post-only flag can still match as a taker, pay the taker fee and earn no rebate. Velocity's docs call this the most common way a market-making strategy quietly loses its rebate. (medium confidence)

On Jupiter's JLP markets, 75% of all fees go to the JLP pool and 25% to Jupiter as protocol revenue. The fees include open and close fees, price impact, borrow fees and swap fees. Beta markets run on a separate engine and do not feed the pool. JLP holders are the counterparty to every trader, so the borrow and impact fees are their compensation for bearing trader PnL, not risk-free income. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

A resting order is not automatically a maker. On Velocity an order is a maker only with the post-only flag; without it a resting order can still match as a taker, pay the taker fee and earn no rebate. Jupiter's Beta trade form labels the fee as an estimate: the fee actually charged follows how the order filled. On Phoenix a limit order is taker on the crossed portion and maker on any remainder that rests. (high confidence)

Jupiter's orderbook Beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC, stock perps) drop the base, price impact and borrow fees. They charge taker or maker fees and an hourly funding rate applied on the hour (UTC). Liquidation returns leftover collateral instead of taking all of it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

On Velocity the taker pays a tiered fee on filled notional and the maker earns a rebate paid out of that fee. The fee is denominated in USDT and applied to the position's cost basis rather than billed separately. A round trip pays the taker fee twice. (medium confidence)

Both Jupiter risk advisers frame cost as more than the headline rate. Gauntlet writes tradingFee = (baseFee + orderBookImpact) x tradeSize. Chaos Labs says a fair venue comparison must include opening fees, slippage and liquidation costs, not only borrowing-versus-funding rates, and that Hyperliquid's open interest may include short hedges that rely on stable low funding. (medium confidence)

Hyperliquid's funding is peer-to-peer with no fee collected on payments, and it pays position size x oracle price x funding rate (the oracle price, not the mark price). Jupiter's Beta markets compute each hourly payment on the position value at the time it is applied. (medium confidence)

Velocity lenders earn the borrow rate x utilization minus an insurance-fund factor and a protocol factor, both taken from the deposit-side gain. Borrowers pay the same rate whatever those factors are. Interest compounds through deposit and borrow indices, and no interest accrues at zero utilization. (medium confidence)

Fee tiers key on rolling volume, and the windows differ. Pacifica uses 14-day volume, updated daily, with subaccounts pooled into the master account's tier. Velocity uses trailing 30-day taker plus maker volume; each counter decays linearly to zero over 30 days, a fill's volume promotes the very next fill, and liquidation volume counts for both sides. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jupiter's fee page lists the Solana transaction cost as a SOL network fee plus a priority fee that Jupiter sets automatically; the trade form has no priority-fee or Jito-tip setting. Sibling concepts cover those costs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

GUM and Jupiter's Beta markets pay funding every hour, on the hour (UTC), on the position held at that moment. A positive rate means longs pay shorts; a negative rate means shorts pay longs. GUM adds that a position opened and closed between two hourly marks pays no funding, that GUM takes no fee on funding, and that paying funding lowers account value and so moves the position closer to liquidation. Hyperliquid likewise says funding is purely peer-to-peer with no fee collected on the payments. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
